The gap

Most CRMs were built to sell software seats.

They assume a thirty-day cycle, one buyer and a published price list. None of that describes a $312,000 retrofit sold into a plant that cannot stop running.

01

Your biggest quotes are built in a spreadsheet.

A retrofit is forty configurable lines, tiered discounts, a service contract and three approvals. No deal field holds that - so it is priced outside the CRM, sent as a PDF, and the pipeline is later told a single total nobody can trace back.

02

The deal history sits in one rep's inbox.

Reps sell out of Outlook and off plant floors. Logging a call means re-typing a conversation into a web form afterwards - the same job done twice - so it is skipped, and whoever covers the account next opens the record and finds nothing.

03

Ask for the forecast, get three different numbers.

The rep's dashboard, the manager's export and the board pack each apply their own filters, date rules and exclusions. Every one of them is defensible. No two of them agree, and the meeting is spent negotiating the number instead of acting on it.

iCRM starts at the other end - the quote, the inbox, and one number every report reads.

02
2 Analyse

Sixty open things. Which one is worth Monday morning?

Every CRM hands you a to-do list. None of them tell you which item actually moves money this week. Action Items scores your entire book - and then shows its working: the chips on each row are the reason it ranked there, so a rep can argue with the list instead of ignoring it.

  • Deterministic scoring - no model, no black box, nothing you can't audit
  • Every weight is yours to set. The ranking is your sales policy, written down
  • One button per row does the whole action; every count opens exactly the rows it counted

03
3 Quote

The deal is won in the quote. So why does it live in Excel?

Forty configurable lines, tiered discounts, a service contract and three signatures - no wonder the real selling happens in a spreadsheet, and the pipeline number is a guess. iCPQ is a seven-step builder inside the CRM: same records, same permissions, same audit trail, and a link the customer opens without a login.

  • What the customer sees is a separate decision from what the quote records
  • No approval needed? Then it's one button, not two - and the button says so
  • Editing a line tomorrow never reshapes the document already sitting in their inbox

Trust & control

Every number a person sees is a number they can open.

Visibility is a security boundary, not a display filter. A rep's dashboard, a manager's report and an export all resolve through the same scope - which is why they finally agree.

  • Four role tiers and per-action permission keys - never a role name hard-coded in a condition
  • Scope of own, team or everything, set per user, on reads and writes independently
  • Single-tenant: one organisation per database, no shared multi-tenant row space
  • SOC 2-aligned controls, encrypted by default, granular role-based access

Why ITHENA

Not a horizontal CRM with a manufacturing skin.

The same team that builds MES, CMMS and shopfloor systems builds this. Plants, assets, after-market service and spare parts are first-class records rather than a "custom object" bent into the shape of a compressor - and pre-built accelerators mean you start from a configured CRM, not an empty one.

Quoting is the core, not an add-on
iCPQ ships in the same product, on the same records. The complex quote stops being the reason your pipeline data is wrong - because it stops living in a spreadsheet the CRM never sees.
Single-tenant, secure by design
One organisation per deployment - your data doesn't share a database with anyone else's, and there is no tenant switch to get wrong. SOC 2-aligned controls, encrypted by default, granular role-based access and an append-only audit trail. Reach is set per user - own, team or everything - and it decides every list, every stat and every export alike.
ERP-adjacent, not ERP-hostile
ITHENA already builds the ERP integrations. Third-party record IDs live in a dedicated link table rather than bolted onto your business records, so the integration can change without your CRM's data model changing.
It works inside Gmail and Outlook
A sidebar puts the record beside the thread, so a conversation is logged where it was read - against the contact, the company and the deal in one click, not re-typed into a web form that evening. Open tracking is opt-in per email, and a contact who has opted out is never sent a pixel.
One forecast number, three audiences
The rep's pipeline, the manager's roll-up and the board slide come off the same scoped query - a rep sees their slice, an admin sees the org, from one definition. Dashboards are built rather than requested, and every one resolves through that same scope, so two tiles cannot disagree about the same deals.
Sales visits, filled in on the floor
Every view is usable from 375px up with nothing gated behind screen size, and it installs as a PWA. The sales-visit form is the one screen designed for the phone first - full-width fields, targets you can hit with a glove on, no hover-only controls.

Questions

Before you book the call

Do we have to replace our ERP?
No. iCRM sits in front of it. ITHENA already builds ERP integrations as a product line, and third-party record IDs are held in a dedicated link table rather than bolted onto your business records - so the integration can change without the CRM's data model changing.
Where is the pricing page?
There isn't one. Each deployment is a single tenant scoped to your plants, your modules and your integration surface, so a per-seat number on a web page would be a guess. A scoping call gives you a real one.
How complex a quote can it actually handle?
Configurable line items with per-line billing terms, effective-dated price books, tiered and per-line discounting, multi-step approval routing, and branded document sections. What the customer's printed document shows is a separate decision from what the quote records - so editing a line later never reshapes a quote already sitting in someone's inbox.
Does it work on a phone?
Every view is usable from 375px up, with no feature gated behind screen size, and it installs as a PWA. The sales visit form in particular is built mobile-first, for people filling it in on a plant floor.
What happens to our existing CRM data?
Accounts, contacts, opportunities and activity history migrate, with duplicate candidates surfaced on import rather than merged silently. Migration scope is part of the scoping call - it's usually the item that decides the timeline.
